headline: Check Daily Missile Range Closure Schedules
reservation: White Sands National Park does not currently require a timed-entry reservation for general day visits. However, the park and Highway 70 may close for up to three hours during missile tests; check the official NPS site for daily closure alerts.

days.title: Introduction to Gypsum Dunes

stops.name: Interdune Boardwalk
stops.detail: Walk the elevated path to learn about the fragile gypsum ecosystem without climbing dunes.

stops.name: Dunes Drive
stops.detail: Drive the eight-mile route through the heart of the dunefield to see the landscape transform into pure white.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; the road transitions from pavement to hard-packed gypsum.
days.note: Check the visitor center for current wind alerts before walking far from your vehicle.

days.title: Desert Life and Sledding

stops.name: Dune Life Nature Trail
stops.detail: Hike this moderate one-mile loop to see animal tracks and desert vegetation at the dune edge; expect soft sand and steep dune climbs.

stops.name: Heart of the Sands
stops.detail: Find a steep slope away from the road for sand sledding on the cool gypsum.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; travel is local within the park boundaries.
days.note: Midday heat can be intense even in shoulder seasons; carry at least one gallon of water per person.

days.title: The Backcountry Experience

stops.name: Alkali Flat Trail
stops.detail: Follow the red diamond trail markers across strenuous dunes toward Alkali Flat, the dry bed of ancient Lake Otero; this is not a route to Lake Lucero.

stops.name: Playa Trail
stops.detail: Visit this level trail to see how seasonal water shapes the desert floor.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; ensure you have enough fuel as there is no gas in the park.
days.note: Navigation is difficult in shifting sand; do not rely on footprints and always follow the official trail posts.

intel.title: Dunes Drive Pullouts
intel.text: Parking is available in designated lots along the loop. Do not park on the gypsum road surface itself as it can be soft and prone to trapping vehicles.

intel.title: GPS Reliability
intel.text: Cellular service is intermittent within the dunefield. Download the official NPS app and maps for offline use before arriving at the park gate.

intel.title: Alamogordo Supplies
intel.text: Fill your tank and buy all drinking water in Alamogordo or Las Cruces. There are no gas stations or water bottle filling stations along Dunes Drive.

intel.title: Missile Range Closures
intel.text: Access can be blocked for several hours due to nearby White Sands Missile Range activity. Always check the official park Facebook or NPS alert page the morning of your visit.

intel.title: Park Closing Times
intel.text: The park has strict closing hours and gates are locked nightly. Ensure you allow 20 minutes to drive from the heart of the dunes back to the Highway 70 exit.

plan.arrival: Pick up a rental at Las Cruces International Airport (LRU) and drive 75 minutes to Alamogordo to secure water, sun protection, and a sand sled.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are suitable for the packed-gypsum Dunes Drive; check rental terms for driving on unpaved surfaces.
plan.goldenHour: The Sunset Stroll area provides a named viewpoint for evening light, though actual timing varies significantly by month.
